items.title: George Guesnon Interview, 1965-09
items.q: He's Uncle Tom. He's everything else, you see.

ctx.x: Yeah. The piano player can read and he plays it, the note by note on the piano, and I learn the melody and then I put your things to it, you see.

Yeah. The pretty thing, man. You see, what made the song so important, because years ago this was a great event. Oh, man, people, wait, no, the king of the Zulus on Mardi Gras, you see, but with civil rights and all that, he's become an obsolete thing. Nobody don't want him around. He's Uncle Tom. He's everything else, you see. Yeah, yeah. But in the days that I'm telling you about, man, people waited for him. Yeah. And he came out, he took, you know, had king Rex. You see, like I say, even though he doesn't wear…
I bet it was. That was in the 20s. Oh, yeah, that's what it is.
